```{r}
#| label: data
#| include: false
#| echo: false

load(file = here("input/data/proc/df_balanced.RData"))

glimpse(df_balanced)

# Generate analytical sample

df_study1 <- df_balanced %>%
  select(-muestra) %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(ola = case_when(ola == 1 ~ 1,
                         ola == 2 ~ 2, 
                         ola == 3 ~ 3,
                         ola == 4 ~ 4,
                         ola == 6 ~ 5,
                         ola == 7 ~ 6)) %>% 
  mutate(ola = as.factor(ola),
         ola_num = as.numeric(ola),
         ola_2=as.numeric(ola)^2)

df_study1 <- df_study1 %>%
  group_by(idencuesta) %>%             # Agrupar por el identificador del participante
  mutate(n_participaciones = n()) %>%  # Contar el número de filas (participaciones) por participante
  ungroup()

df_study1 <- df_study1 %>% filter(n_participaciones>1)

# Corregir etiquetas

df_study1$just_pension <- sjlabelled::set_label(df_study1$just_pension, 
                        label = "Pension distributive justice")

df_study1$egp <- sjlabelled::set_label(df_study1$egp, 
                        label = "Social class")

df_study1$merit_effort <- sjlabelled::set_label(df_study1$merit_effort, 
                        label = "People are rewarded for their efforts")

df_study1$merit_talent <- sjlabelled::set_label(df_study1$merit_talent, 
                        label = "People are rewarded for their intelligence")


```

# Methodology {background-color="#491106ff"}

## Data

::: {.incremental .highlight-last style="font-size: 120%;"}

- [ELSOC (COES)](https://coes.cl/elsoc/): a representative panel survey of the urban adult population in Chile, based on a probabilistic, stratified, clustered, and multistage sampling design across large and small cities

- Period: six waves (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, and 2023)

- Attrition 2016→2023: ~ 40%

- Analytical sample (**balanced 6-wave panel**): 

    * **N = 7,522 observations** (level 1) nested within 
    * **N = 1,317 individuals** (level 2)

:::

::: {.incremental style="font-size: 100%;"}

- Item: **¿"It is fair that people with higher incomes have better pensions than people with lower incomes?"**

:::

::: {.notes}

- the dependent variable is preferences for market justice in pensions, measured with the item "It is fair that people with higher incomes have better pensions than people with lower incomes?" (5-point Likert scale)

- as we observe in the alluvial diagram, there is a clear trend towards more agreement with market justice in pensions, changing from 17% in 2016 to 29.4% in 2023, representing an increase of about 60%.

:::



## Independent variables: Level 1

```{r}
#| label: fig-merit
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of responses for meritocracy items"
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: '90%'
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| echo: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

df_plot <- df_study1 %>%
  dplyr::select(merit_effort, merit_talent) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    item = factor(
      item,
      levels = c("merit_talent","merit_effort"),
      labels = c(
         "People are rewarded for their \nintelligence and ability",
        "People are rewarded for their efforts"
      )
    ),
    value = factor(
      as.character(value),
      levels = c(
        "Strongly disagree",
        "Disagree",
        "Neither agree nor disagree",
        "Agree",
        "Strongly agree"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  drop_na(value) %>%
  count(item, value) %>%
  group_by(item) %>%
  mutate(
    p = n / sum(n),
    label = percent(p, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = item, y = p, fill = value)) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Strongly disagree" = "#CA0020",
      "Disagree" = "#F4A582",
      "Neither agree nor disagree" = "gray65",
      "Agree" = "#92C5DE",
      "Strongly agree" = "#0571B0"
    ),
    breaks = c(
      "Strongly disagree",
      "Disagree",
      "Neither agree nor disagree",
      "Agree",
      "Strongly agree"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Source: own elaboration with data from ELSOC 2016-2023 (N obs = 7,522; N individuals = 1,317)"
  ) +
  theme_ggdist(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


```




## Independent variables: Level 2


```{r}
#| label: fig-class
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| fig-cap: "Frecuency of class position"
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: '90%'
#| fig-asp: 0.6
#| echo: false

df_study1 %>%
  count(egp) %>%
  mutate(prop = (n / sum(n))*100) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(egp = fct_rev(egp)) %>% 
  ggplot(
    aes(x = egp, y = prop, group = egp, fill = egp)
  ) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = .9, alpha = 1, show.legend = F) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 40), 
                       breaks = seq(0, 40, 10),
                       labels = function(prop){paste0(prop, "%")},
                       expand = c(0,1)) +
  MetBrewer::scale_fill_met_d("VanGogh2") +
  coord_flip()+
  geom_text(mapping = aes(label = scales::percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1, decimal.mark = ",")),
              hjust = -0.2,
              fontface = "bold",
              size = 4,
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  labs(
    title = "Class position based on EGP scheme",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Source: own elaboration with data from ELSOC 2016-2023 (N obs = 7,522; N individuals = 1,317)"
  ) +
  theme_ggdist(base_size = 16)+
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

```


    
- Fixed at the first wave (i.e., time-invariant) → captures average between-person differences (BE = $\bar X_{i}$)



## Estimation strategy

:::: {.incremental style="font-size: 110%;"}

**Cumulative link mixed models (CLMM)**:

- Panel structure: repeated observations (level 1) nested within individuals (level 2)

- Models both _within-person_ (WE) and _between-person_ (BE) effects; includes random effects (intercept and time slope) 

- WE/BE decomposition (person-mean centering) [@bell_fixed_2019]: 

     * Within: $X^{WE}_{it}= X_{it}-\bar{X}_i$
     * Between: $X^{BE}_{i}=\bar{X}_i$

- Formally:  

::: {.fragment}
$$\begin{aligned}
\eta_{it} = \beta_{0}+ \beta_{1}\,\text{Time}_{it} +\beta_2\,\text{Meritocracy}^{WE}_{it} +\beta_3\,\text{Meritocracy}^{BE}_{i} +\beta_4\,\mathrm{Class}^{BE}_i +
    \end{aligned}$$
    
$$\beta_5\,(\mathrm{Class}^{BE}_i\!\times\! \text{Meritocracy}^{WE}_{it}) +\beta_6\,(\mathrm{Class}^{BE}_i\!\times\! \text{Meritocracy}^{BE}_{i}) +u_{0i}+u_{1i}\,\text{Time}_{it}\\$$
:::
